Evaluation reports go to NMED within fifteen days. This is a transfer requirement, not a universal pre-offer evaluation. Seller shall provide records and meet required compliance before closing; buyer may terminate before settlement if required transfer compliance is not achieved, subject to lawful return of deposits. No unauthorized entry or occupancy is permitted while residual contamination remains subject to the notice. A signed purchase agreement or generic packet status does not certify cleanup, authorize entry or submit notices to NMED. Seller must comply before transfer; known contamination is not made harmless by an as-is provision. Closing shall verify recorded legal description, ownership, title insurance, community-property/spousal joinder and acknowledged deed requirements. Seller-owned appurtenant water rights intended to convey shall be expressly identified in the deed unless lawfully reserved; provide OSE records and perform applicable county/OSE ownership updates. A well or irrigation use does not by itself establish transferable water rights. Review shared-well agreements, acequia/ditch obligations, legal access and local permits during inspection. The existing seller tax valuation is not a guarantee of buyer taxes. Federal and state withholding and sales-information reporting remain the closing agent responsibilities.

entries.residential_sale_propertyConditionStatus: This ordinary resale package does not require a universal Wyoming statutory seller condition form before an offer. Seller shall truthfully disclose known material conditions, answer specific inquiries and avoid misrepresentation or active concealment. Any voluntarily supplied condition statement remains separate from this agreement and is not a warranty or independent inspection. Licensed agent adverse-material-fact and relationship duties under W.S. 33-28-303 and 33-28-306 apply when such professionals participate; they do not make this FSBO platform a broker. This agreement does not add a broad as-is waiver of fraud or other available remedies.
entries.residential_sale_statutoryPacketStatus_h: Verify water and irrigation rights with the State Engineer, including permits, adjudication, well access and any deed reservations or severance. Under applicable Wyoming water law, identify seller-owned appurtenant rights intended to convey rather than infer ownership from a visible well or ditch. Seller shall provide existing records; title and closing professionals shall complete required transfers and ownership updates. Review mineral/surface estates, easements, physical/legal access, shared wells and development restrictions during inspection. No new water test or radon test is universally required solely by this agreement. For on-site wastewater, obtain existing permits and disclose known defects, then comply with DEQ or delegated county requirements that actually apply. Do not assume a statewide inspection is required for every resale or make a septic upload universally block an offer. Agree any additional inspections within the stated inspection period; required health/environmental compliance and undisclosed hazards remain separate from optional reports. Closing shall verify the recorded legal description, all necessary owners and homestead spouse signatures, marketable title, liens, acknowledged deed and applicable county/state reporting. Prepare the required statement of consideration and other recording documents; this contract does not replace them. Provide applicable HOA covenants, dues, assessments and transfer information under the actual governing documents; this package does not invent a universal HOA cooling-off period. Apply federal lead and withholding requirements where applicable and use property Mountain time with daylight saving for deadlines.
entries.residential_sale_hoaDocumentsStatus_help: Provide property-specific governing documents, fees and assessments. Developer condominium sales are outside this resale workflow.
